quiz.q: Why wrap a money transfer in a transaction?
options: So both updates happen or neither does
quiz.explain: A transaction makes the two changes all-or-nothing, so money never appears or disappears.
ROLLBACK throws away all changes made inside the current transaction.

quiz.q: After an error inside BEGIN, the next statements say `current transaction is aborted`. What now?
options: ROLLBACK (or COMMIT, which rolls back) and start again
quiz.explain: Once a statement fails, the transaction can only be ended. Postgres ignores everything until then.

options: Is its own tiny transaction, saved immediately
quiz.explain: By default Postgres autocommits each statement on its own.

flashcards.back: All-or-nothing, rules always hold, others don't see half-done work, committed means saved.
